sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains two interpretations of "Hashem is Elokim": first, that the concealment of Elokim is actually from Hashem, and second, that even the name Hashem is a mere garment relative to the Essence.

translations.translation: And the explanation is,
behold, "Hashem is Elokim" has two interpretations and concepts.
The first is that even the tzimtzum of Elokim is Hashem.
For, behold, Hashem is a term meaning "He who brings into being,"
for all coming into being is from the name Hashem,
except that in order for the coming into being to be actualized in the aspect of a separate entity and thing,
behold, this is through the name Elokim, which conceals and hides the name Hashem,
as it is written,
"For a sun and a shield is Hashem Elokim."
And this is "Hashem is Elokim,"
that although the coming into being in actuality and revelation is from the name Elokim, as it is written,
"In the beginning Elokim created the heavens and the earth,"
and thirty-two times Elokim is said in the account of creation,
as a result of which the world became a separate entity and thing,
behold, regarding this comes the commandment "And you shall know... that Hashem is Elokim,"
that even the name Elokim, which constricts and conceals, is Hashem,
for Hashem and Elokim are entirely one,
and therefore in truth
(as it is relative to the Holy One, blessed be He)
it does not conceal at all,
and through the service of Torah and mitzvos, they draw down the revelation of the name Hashem into the world.
For this is what is written, "which Elokim created to do,"
"to do" meaning to rectify,
that one must rectify the concealment of the name Elokim and draw down the revelation of the name Hashem into the world,
as it is written
(afterwards)
"on the day that Hashem Elokim made earth and heavens,"
where the name Hashem is also mentioned here.
For through the service of man,
"to work it and to guard it"
(Torah and mitzvos),
the revelation of the name Hashem is drawn into the world,
and it becomes "These are the generations of the heavens and the earth...,"
"generations" spelled fully,
and even to "These are the generations of Peretz,"
"generations" spelled fully,
which is a higher level even than "These are the generations of the heavens and the earth,"
for through the service of Torah and mitzvos, they break through all the concealments and veils of the name Elokim,
and make a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He, in the lower realms.
And the second concept in "Hashem is Elokim" is,
that even the name Hashem
(as it is above its investment in the name Elokim)
is only an aspect of Elokim and tzimtzum relative to His Essence and Being, blessed be He, as it were,
and as it is written,
"I am Hashem, that is My name," that the aspect of Hashem is only a name,
a radiance and illumination alone,
which is a great and immense tzimtzum relative to the light of the Ein Sof Himself, blessed be He, as it were.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the two interpretations correspond to the service of the righteous and of baalei teshuvah, where teshuvah draws from above the name Hashem.

translations.translation: And behold, these two concepts are drawn through the two services of the righteous and of baalei teshuvah.
For when a person is in a state of "Elokim made man upright,"
behold, through his service in Torah and mitzvos he draws the revelation of the name Hashem into the name Elokim
(the first concept in "Hashem is Elokim"),
as above
(section 3).
But when he sinned and blemished and perverted the path, it is impossible for him to draw from the aspect of Hashem
(since he blemished the name Hashem),
and he must draw from an aspect that is above the name Hashem.
And this drawing is through the service of teshuvah.
For all the matters above are drawn specifically through service.
And even the drawing of the Ein Sof that is above the chain of descent, which no arousal from below reaches there,
does not dwell and become revealed
(in an aspect of inwardness)
except when there is perfection in the actions of the lower beings,
for the Holy One, blessed be He, does not dwell except in a complete place.
And this drawing
(of the Ein Sof that is above the chain of descent)
is through the service that is above the chain of descent
(in man),
the service of teshuvah.
For when one does teshuvah, and particularly such that intentional sins become for him like merits,
which is teshuvah from love, from the depth of the heart, with great love, as explained in Tanya,
behold, through this he arouses from an aspect that is above the name Hashem,
relative to which even Hashem is considered like Elokim,
the second concept in "Hashem is Elokim."
[And this is the advantage of teshuvah in its simple sense over the teshuvah of Shabbos, the letters of "Shabbos" being "tashev" (you shall return),
for the teshuvah
(and the ascent)
of Shabbos, the letters of which are "tashev," is only the matter of "And Elokim completed,"
that the measure of tzimtzum and concealment of the name Elokim ceases and the revelation of the name Hashem is drawn,
but in order to arouse from an aspect that is above the name Hashem,
behold, this is done through teshuvah in its simple sense,
and particularly through such teshuvah that intentional sins become for him like merits,
for through the refinement and transformation of intentional sins, an advantage of light is made.
And all the more so from what is brought in the Zohar,
that the matter of the Giving of the Torah was done specifically through the admission of Yisro, "Now I know that Hashem is greater than all the gods,"
even though in the Giving of the Torah it is said "Anochi"
(only)
once,
all the more so the matter of "Anochi Anochi" twice,
that its drawing is specifically through the refinement and transformation of darkness.
And in the manner explained in Tanya,
that the ultimate perfection that will be in the days of Moshiach,
a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He, in the lower realms,
depends
(primarily)
on our deeds and service during the time of exile specifically].
And after the arousal from above Hashem
(through teshuvah)
one must draw down
from above to below into the aspect of Hashem, a term meaning "He who brings into being,"
and even to the aspect of Hashem as it is invested in the name Elokim,
the first concept in "Hashem is Elokim."
And this is why in teshuvah it is said twice "Hashem is Elokim,"
that at first it is the matter of ascent from below to above until, relative to it, Hashem is considered like Elokim
(the second interpretation of "Hashem is Elokim"),
and afterwards the drawing down from above to below in Hashem, a term meaning "He who brings into being,"
and as it is invested in the name Elokim
(the first interpretation of "Hashem is Elokim"),
from which comes the coming into being in actuality,
"In the beginning Elokim created the heavens and the earth,"
and not only the drawing into the Sefiros
(according to the explanation of the Zohar
that "In the beginning..." refers to the Sefiros),
but also into the heavens and the earth and all their hosts, in their simple sense.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the two concepts correspond to the two aspects of the shofar: the inner voice arousing the Essence, and the physical shofar drawing down into the lowest levels.

translations.translation: And this is also the two concepts
in the blowing of the shofar
(which alludes to the matter of teshuvah),
that the sound of the shofar is an inner voice
(the aspect of the inwardness of the heart)
and together with this one must blow specifically with a physical shofar,
for on Rosh Hashanah all things return to their primordial state,
and through the shofar they arouse a new drawing from the Awtsmoos.
For shofar is the aspect of Binah, which is above the chain of descent,
the aspect of will that is above even the aspect of Binah,
and higher still, a new drawing from the inwardness and Essence of the Holy One, blessed be He,
and from there it is drawn into the aspect of the inwardness of the will,
into the inwardness of Binah, etc., until the inwardness of the worlds,
and from this is afterwards drawn also into the externality of the worlds,
as explained in the Siddur,
in the discourse "To understand the matter of the blowing of the shofar according to the intention of the Baal Shem Tov, of blessed memory."
And therefore the shofar has the two aforementioned concepts,
through the inner voice of the shofar,
the aspect of the inwardness of the heart,
they arouse the Essence,
and through the blowing with a physical shofar,
and specifically with a shofar of an animal,
and moreover that the horn of the shofar must be detached
(and not attached to the animal),
the aspect of the inanimate,
through this they draw down below into Asiyah, even to the aspect of the inanimate.
And as we say in the Rosh Hashanah prayer, "And every formed being shall know that You are its Former,"
that even in Asiyah
(as brought in the writings of the Ariza"l,
that "every formed being" refers to the world of Asiyah),
and even the inanimate in Asiyah,
shall know that You are its Former.
